samples.prompt: Write a candid reflection on the gap between public perception and private reality, using humor and irony to explore personal vanity.
samples.generated:
I do not know whether I am to be blamed for that which is said of me.  For if there is any one thing in which I am distinguished, it is that I have never pretended to be anything but what I was;--and there is no man who pretends to be himself, and who has not something of merit to boast of.

And yet it may not be altogether true, that this is my only fault.  It is quite possible that, in some of those little things which are so important in the lives of women, I may have been deceived by appearances, and mistaken the truth.  But I have always been conscious of a strong feeling of indignation against such deception; and I do not see why I should have been less angry with myself than I should with another person.

But if there is anything which I think myself deserving of blame, it is that I have not kept up the same appearance at all times.  I did not know that people were so particular as to dress themselves properly.  I thought that it was perfectly natural to go about without a coat on, when it was hot; and that if you did so, you could take your dinner and walk to church and take your breakfast after church and go to bed, without ever taking off your shirt, or even changing it.
